newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court rejects harsher penalties for Chun, Roh.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court rejects harsher penalties for Chun, Roh.

text.p: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday rejected prosecution appeals against reduced sentences for former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo over a 1979 coup and an army massacre the following year.
It upheld a lower appeals court decision in December to commute Chun's death sentence to life in jail and Roh's 22-1/2 year prison term to 17 years for mutiny and treason.
Both ex-presidents were also convicted in the original "trial of the century" last year of corruption for amassing hundreds of millions of dollars in slush funds while in office.
President Kim Young-sam is widely expected to offer his predecessors a pardon before he steps down from office next February.
A presidential spokesman said this week he was not aware of any amnesty plan.

Chief justice Yoon Kwan, leading a panel of judges in the highest appeals court in the land, also upheld the sentences on 12 former generals for their roles in one of the darkest chapters of South Korean history.

The 1979 coup thrust Chun to power and the massacre of pro-democracy activists in the southwestern city of Kwangju, in which about 200 people died by official count, crushed opposition to the coup leaders.
Chun was president from 1980-1988 and Roh succeeded him, stepping down in 1993.
The 12 generals were jailed for between 3-1/2 years and eight years. Another former general jailed for eight years for mutiny and treason died earlier this month.

The Supreme Court also passed judgement on appeals by several leading tycoons convicted of bribing Roh, including Kim Woo-choong, founder of the giant Daewoo Group, and Choi Won-suk, chairman of the Dong Ah Group.
The court confirmed a two-year suspended jail sentence for Kim and a 2-1/2 year suspended jail term on Choi Won-suk.
Kim's sentence was suspended for three years by the lower appeals court and Choi's for four years.
The court rejected a prosecution appeal against the acquittal of Chung Tae-soo, the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group, who was also charged with topping up Roh's slush fund.
Chung is standing trial on separate charges of bribery in connection with the collapse in January of the Hanbo Group's steelmaking flagship in a loans scandal.
The court confirmed the acquittal of Lee Kyung-hoon, former president of Daewoo Corp, Daewoo Group's trading arm. Prosecutors had challenged the acquittal.

Chun's death sentence was commuted by the Seoul High Court in recognition of his role in the fast-paced economic development of the Asian "Tiger" and the peaceful transfer of the presidency to Roh in 1988.
Chun and Roh defended the 1979 military takeover as needed to quell civil insurrection that they said risked exposing capitalist South Korea to attack from the communist North.
